case_name: Lakhiya Devi and another v Girja Yadav and Others
facts: Both these appeals arise out of the judgment and order passed by the Patna High Court in Criminal Appeal No.43 of 1982.
The prosecution case was that during the night between 6th and 7th April, 1976 Chander Yadav was at his 'Khalihan' situated at a little distance from the village.

At about 6 O'clock in the morning, he came running to his house and after getting the main entrance door opened, he went into a small room where foodgrains used to be stored and closed its door from inside.
The assailants were either armed with sticks and sharp weapons.
Lakhiya Devi tried to prevent them from carrying away the dead body by catching hold of it but accused Saudagar pushed her away by giving a kick on her chest.
When her daughter-in-law Shanti Devi tried to prevent them from taking away the dead body she was also pushed aside and threatened.
The assailants then carried the dead body of Chander with them by scaling over the western boundary wall of his house and were proceeding towards the west of the village.
At that time two police constables, Shanker Dayal and Kapil Kumar, on being informed about what had happened, ran after the assailants.
issues: Whether the High Court was correct in acquitting the accused except Budhai under Section 326 read with Section 149 IPC and that of Budhai under Section 325 read with Section 149 IPC
Whether the evidence of the eye-witnesses should be relied upon
petitioner_arguments: The High Court committed a grave error in acquitting the accused as stated above and that has also led to failure of justice.

The High Court having believed that murder of Chander was committed inside his house in that small room, that the door of that room was broken open and that the accused had then carried away the dead body by dragging it, ought to have believed that the accused were also the murders and should have convicted all of them under Section 302 read with Section 149 IPC.
respondent_arguments: Even though it is possible to take a different view on re-appreciation of the evidence, this Court should not interfere with the order of acquittal, as it cannot be said that the view taken by the High Court is perverse or so unreasonable as to justify interference by this Court.
court_reasoning: The High Court was wrong in rejecting the evidence of the eye-witnesses on the ground that they had exaggerated the manner in which injuries were caused to Chander.
Moreover, the findings recorded by it are inconsistent inasmuch as it has believed the prosecution evidence that after Chander was killed the accused had carried away the dead body from the house.

If accused were the persons who had carried away the dead body of Chander from that small room of his house then surely they were the persons who had entered the house of Chander and in all probability they were the persons who killed him.
holding: The appeals are allowed. The conviction of the accused under Section 201 IPC is confirmed. The notice issued for alteration of their conviction for the higher offence and enhancement of sentence is also discharged.
cases_cited: Lakhiya Devi and another v Girja Yadav
